milestones.title: Planning
milestones.description: Review requirements, security design and architecture before application implementation.

milestones.title: M0 — Feasibility
milestones.description: Validate portable deployment, hosting, SMTP, storage, protocol and media with documented evidence.

milestones.title: M1 — Foundation
milestones.description: Approved workspace, CI, Docker, configuration and bilingual public site.

milestones.title: M2 — Temporary rooms
milestones.description: Verified encrypted group text, in-memory lifecycle, expiry and abuse controls.

milestones.title: M3 — Managed accounts
milestones.description: Provisioning, first-login change, MFA, sessions and authorized administrator inbox.

milestones.title: M4 — Persistent messaging and media
milestones.description: Encrypted history and attachments, direct voice recording and recovery behavior.

milestones.title: M5 — Web release
milestones.description: Security review, accessibility, deployment, restore and accurate release documentation.

milestones.title: M6 — Mobile
milestones.description: Android and PWA enhancements; evaluate deferred iOS feasibility.

issues.title: Documentation and community readiness
issues.summary: Establish reviewable requirements, public decisions and contribution rules before implementing the application.
issues.scope: Public documentation, traceability and community workflow; no automatic acceptance of product drafts.
acceptance: SRS preserves every PRD ID and distinguishes proposals from accepted decisions.
Contribution, publication and review policies are reviewable without private handoffs.
Initial backlog and owner-run GitHub setup are documented; remote creation is reported separately.

issues.title: Technical feasibility evidence
issues.summary: Prove candidate deployment, resource and browser assumptions with bounded experiments.
issues.scope: Synthetic-data experiments after authorization; no production service or secure-release claim.
acceptance: Each experiment has a question, budget, environment and repeatable procedure.
Results record limitations and determine supported profiles and draft limits.
Failures trigger explicit decisions rather than mandatory BaaS or unsupported free-host claims.

issues.title: Portable bilingual foundation
issues.summary: Prepare an approved workspace and deployable bilingual foundation without duplicating backend logic.
issues.scope: Architecture and foundation work after decision/feasibility gates; no chat features in this epic.
acceptance: Accepted boundaries separate frontend and backend responsibilities.
Clean builds, runtime public config and Docker profiles are reproducible.
Arabic/English routing and RTL/LTR start in foundation work.

issues.title: Encryption and participant key lifecycle
issues.summary: Resolve authenticated encryption, device/history access and recovery before secure messaging implementation.
issues.scope: Threat model, established protocol evaluation and recovery UX; no home-grown protocol or automatic audit claim.
acceptance: Protocol and library assessment covers temporary groups and managed history.
Key custody, new/lost devices, resets and administrator continuity are explicit.
Review and negative/interoperability evidence requirements are defined.

issues.title: Docker and self-hosting operations
issues.summary: Make local and future production deployment portable with explicit persistence and isolation.
issues.scope: Development dependencies now; full app/proxy/backup profiles after application runtime decisions.
acceptance: Local dependency configuration validates and remains separate from production claims.
Temporary isolation and managed volume/restore boundaries have accepted decisions.
Future clean-install and restore tests are specified and later executed.

issues.title: Temporary private text rooms
issues.summary: Deliver verified accountless encrypted group text with terminal expiry and no durable history.
issues.scope: Future P0 room flow after crypto, verification and lifecycle decisions; no media or replay.
acceptance: Room creation, owner authority and encrypted multi-participant flows meet the SRS.
Normal, failure and restart inspections cover temporary non-persistence.
Abuse and deadline controls have bounded-resource evidence.

issues.title: Managed persistent messaging
issues.summary: Deliver authorized administrator-to-user conversations with encrypted durable history.
issues.scope: Future P0 message/history flow; read receipts, replies, search and export remain P1.
acceptance: Membership, uniqueness and durable acknowledgment are enforced across APIs/events.
Authorized keys recover history through tested restart/restore behavior.
Cross-user access and reset/key-loss cases behave as specified.

issues.title: Voice recording and playback
issues.summary: Deliver direct microphone recording and authorized encrypted voice playback in managed chat.
issues.scope: Future P0 record/preview/send/play/pause/seek with localized failures; no calls or temporary media.
acceptance: Supported client matrix passes recording and playback scenarios.
Cancel, permission, quota and corruption failures are handled.
Voice content uses the same authorized private storage and key lifecycle as managed attachments.

issues.title: Review public and private repository boundaries
issues.summary: Review ignore rules and public decision references before publishing local documentation.
issues.scope: Secrets, private handoffs, runtime data and build contexts; keep source migrations and synthetic fixtures trackable.
acceptance: git check-ignore covers sensitive representative paths and permits intended public files.
No public document links to an ignored private handoff.
Original private files remain local and unchanged; tracked history limitations are documented.

issues.title: Review contribution standards and GitHub templates
issues.summary: Adopt consistent stories/tasks, comments, branch names, commit messages and PR review expectations.
issues.scope: Contribution guide, conduct policy, issue/PR forms, field definitions and definitions of ready/done.
acceptance: Examples use English technical content and real requirement references.
Templates request acceptance and failure/privacy cases without requiring private evidence.
Policy recommendations are not described as enabled branch/CI enforcement.

issues.title: Review SRS scope and proposed refinements
issues.summary: Review SRS against PRD and latest owner decisions without silently changing priority.
issues.scope: DEC-11 and SRS-D01 through SRS-D06; retain read/reply/export/PWA priorities pending explicit change.
acceptance: Every PRD requirement remains traceable with its priority.
Owner decisions and provisional technical proposals are distinguished.
Approved changes and still-open points are recorded explicitly.

issues.title: Document the messaging threat model
issues.summary: Describe assets, adversaries, metadata, client trust and temporary non-persistence boundaries.
issues.scope: Malicious host JS, participants, account/session compromise, proxy logs, browser history, swap and backups.
acceptance: Data flows and trust boundaries cover both modes.
Threats have candidate mitigations, residual risks and validation plans.
The model distinguishes client clearing from physical erasure and participant copies.

issues.title: Evaluate established messaging protocols
issues.summary: Compare protocol/library candidates using primary documentation and the approved threat model.
issues.scope: Identity, invite/member authentication, groups, replay, key changes, versions, licenses and browser/mobile support.
acceptance: A comparison records evidence, maintenance and interoperability assumptions.
Recommendation includes consequences and unresolved security questions.
No primitive-only demo or custom envelope is presented as a reviewed messaging protocol.

issues.title: Specify device enrollment and historical key recovery
issues.summary: Decide who can recover old content after device loss, password reset or administrator device replacement.
issues.scope: Participant key custody, enrollment/revocation, history access, backup/recovery material and irreversible loss UX.
acceptance: Resetting credentials is distinguished from recovering message keys.
Chosen recovery model does not silently add server-readable key escrow.
Both Arabic/English loss and recovery outcomes are specified before implementation.

issues.title: Decide temporary runtime isolation
issues.summary: Compare separate runtime entry points with combined hosting under a measured resource budget.
issues.scope: Import boundaries, credentials, DB network access, media mounts, logging, restart and process cost.
acceptance: ADR states alternatives and isolation consequences.
Validation includes actual network/mount permissions, not container naming.
A combined profile cannot claim the stronger separate-process isolation.

issues.title: Specify sessions, MFA and administrator bootstrap
issues.summary: Resolve browser session transport, origins and secure bootstrap/recovery together.
issues.scope: Cookies/tokens, CSRF/CORS/socket origins, rotation/revocation, first-login restrictions and MFA recovery.
acceptance: Same-origin and supported split-origin behavior is explicit.
Disabled-account and credential-reset effects cover live sockets.
No public default administrator password or hidden MFA recovery bypass is introduced.

issues.title: Define verification metadata and retention policy
issues.summary: Specify verification/counter metadata and basic managed retention before public use.
issues.scope: Enabled public OTP default, explicit override, SMTP failure, no permanent email-room mapping, audit and backups.
acceptance: Each retained field has purpose, lifetime, access and cleanup behavior.
Retention disclosure does not silently promote P1 deletion/export UI to P0.
Backup expiry and limits on recipient-copy deletion are explicit.

issues.title: Specify API, event and data invariants
issues.summary: Define versioned contracts before creating application handlers or migrations.
issues.scope: Authorization, error codes, deadline semantics, idempotency, durable ack, paging, envelope bounds and quota/file finalization.
acceptance: Contracts distinguish command acceptance, persisted content and recipient delivery.
SQL/storage invariants cover concurrency, aborts and orphan recovery.
Temporary rooms have no durable data model or replay path.

issues.title: Define browser, accessibility and workload targets
issues.summary: Choose testable support boundaries and exact byte/resource accounting.
issues.scope: Desktop/mobile browser matrix, RTL/LTR, recording codecs, load duration, latency and RPO/RTO targets.
acceptance: Targets identify environments and a reproducible workload.
Client duration/codec targets are separated from enforceable ciphertext bytes.
Draft PRD quotas are not advertised as measured capacity.

issues.title: Review and smoke-test development Docker dependencies
issues.summary: Validate the prepared PostgreSQL/Mailpit Compose file without implying application deployment is complete.
issues.scope: Configuration validation now; explicit later container startup, health, restart persistence and local SMTP checks.
acceptance: Empty credentials fail and configured Compose validates with loopback-only published ports.
Actual startup/restart/mail checks record results after the owner authorizes running containers.
Production app/proxy/secret/backup work remains separately tracked.

issues.title: Review local tooling checks and optional GitHub CI
issues.summary: Verify bootstrap safety and basic repository checks before enabling them remotely.
issues.scope: Offline tests, manifest validation, ignore/link checks and Compose config; no app test coverage claim.
acceptance: Dry-run performs no authentication, network or mutations.
Tests exercise duplicate/retry behavior, state preservation and wrong-account refusal.
CI remains least-privileged and is not described as enforced until published and run.

issues.title: Configure verified community and private reporting channels
issues.summary: Owner verifies repository settings instead of assuming documentation enables them.
issues.scope: Private vulnerability reporting, moderation contact, issue forms, CODEOWNERS, branch rules and Project views/automation.
acceptance: Private intake is tested and policy links reflect availability.
Solo-maintainer rules do not require impossible self-approval.
Enabled checks/views/settings are recorded separately from recommendations.

issues.title: Define portable web runtime configuration
issues.summary: Decide Next.js deployment and public endpoint configuration for reusable artifacts.
issues.scope: Runtime/static trade-offs, public/secret separation, same/split origins and independent PostgreSQL/backend hosting.
acceptance: Design supports changing public endpoints without rebuilding the same frontend artifact.
Backend logic and credentials do not move into frontend code.
Distributed profile validation is defined, with no provider-specific mandatory dependency.

issues.title: Validate a portable hosting candidate
issues.summary: Run bounded synthetic-data deployment experiments only after reviewing the budget and environment.
issues.scope: WebSocket/recycle, remote DB TLS/permissions, durable disk, streaming limits, SMTP and measured resources.
acceptance: Owner approves explicit time/resource bounds before execution.
Official provider claims are dated and separated from actual measurements.
Results identify limitations and migration steps without claiming free hosting is guaranteed.

issues.title: Validate browser crypto and encrypted media compatibility
issues.summary: Test the proposed protocol and supported recording/playback paths on the agreed client matrix.
issues.scope: Budget-approved disposable prototype, no production keys or real private messages.
acceptance: Record permission/failure handling and actual codec compatibility.
Test authorized decryption, corruption rejection, seek strategy and low-memory behavior.
Findings feed ADRs; the prototype is not described as an audited secure implementation.

issues.title: Create a verified temporary text room
issues.summary: As a guest, I want to verify my mailbox and create a time-limited room so that I can invite others without a permanent account.
issues.scope: Future P0 implementation after protocol/verification gates; no temporary attachments or saved history.
acceptance: With public defaults, unverified creation fails and a valid single-use OTP permits bounded creation.
Invitation does not grant owner termination authority; secrets never enter mail or logs.
Expiry/termination reject new joins and sends; Arabic/English errors explain failures.

issues.title: Record and exchange a private voice message
issues.summary: As a provisioned user, I want to record and preview a voice message in my administrator conversation so that I can explain something without typing.
issues.scope: Future authorized encrypted storage and record/playback UI; waveform/speed remain P1.
acceptance: Supported browser records, shows duration, stops, previews and sends; cancellation uploads nothing.
Permission denial, unsupported formats, quota and transfer failures have localized outcomes.
Administrator decrypts/plays/pauses/seeks the recording; another user cannot retrieve it.

issues.title: Access only my administrator conversation
issues.summary: As a provisioned user, I want my retained conversation to be with the administrator only so that I understand who receives my messages.
issues.scope: Future managed history and disclosure; no user discovery or user-to-user messaging.
acceptance: Exactly one conversation per user is enforced under concurrent provisioning.
Foreign conversation, socket and attachment identifiers are denied independently of the UI.
Retention/admin participation and key-loss behavior are explained in both languages.
